property_summary: setSlopes reverts exactly when the kink is 0 or >= 1e27, and succeeds (storing the slopes) otherwise, once the adapter is initialized with an access control that grants access.
Because C's constructor disables initializers, initialize reverts for any argument on a freshly deployed C, and consequently setSlopes also reverts for any input.
On a freshly deployed C (whose constructor disabled initializers), rate() always reverts for any vault and asset, because it makes an external call into an uninitialized/empty vault address.
On a freshly deployed C (initializers disabled), setLimits reverts for any inputs because access control is unset.
On a fresh C, setSlopes always reverts for any asset when the kink is 0 or >= 1e27, and the call is observable as a revert regardless of kink value chosen adversarially within the invalid range.
For any caller authorized via the access control, setSlopes reverts if and only if the kink is 0 or >= 1e27, and succeeds otherwise.
